title: Jacqu Cornon deathbed confession about Brown's 1956 Paris vacuum chamber test

tellings.quote: And if that's not all, we have audio of a deathbed confession from French aerospace executive Jacqu Cornon, who witnessed Brown's successful experiments in a vacuum chamber in 1956 in Paris, explicitly stating he witnessed a positive result.
Schatzkin actually met Jean-Louis Cornillon in April of 2008 in Pennsylvania right before he died.

as_told.title: Cornillon on the positive vacuum test

plain: In Paris in 1956, the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown is said to have tested a device meant to move without propellant inside a vacuum chamber, and a French aerospace executive named Jacques Cornillon, who watched, said near the end of his life that it worked: the tests were "very very tricky," sensitive to "so many things," but "finally, it works. So that was a positive result." Michels says he has audio of this deathbed account and also points to a 12 page report on the test, called the Montgolfier report after the facility, while Cornillon is heard in his own words; in one episode Michels calls him Jean-Louis Cornillon and says a writer named Paul Schatzkin met him in Pennsylvania in April 2008, at 98, rather than in 2009. If true, a working test in a vacuum would rule out the usual explanation that Brown's devices just pushed on air.
